What the numbers say

For the session of Friday, November 20, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (101 Taiwan-listed names: the 100 largest companies by market value plus the 0050 ETF) as risk-off. The TAIEX is below its 50-day average and below its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the high band.

1 of 101 tickers (1%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 28 of 101 (28%) above their 200-day average. Below 30% is the level the model treats as weak breadth, which is enough on its own for a risk-off reading. On the day 0 rose and 101 fell; the median move was −7.93%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Electronics distribution had the strongest average move at −5.21% and Electronic components the weakest at −9.58%, a spread of 4.37 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 2.31 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

54 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (3702, 2347, 2356, 2002, 2324, 2059 and 48 more), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Summed over the 101 names with institutional data, foreign investors' five-day position is net selling of 583,671 lots and investment trusts' is net selling of 267,826 lots (one lot is 1,000 shares). The two groups are on the same side.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-19), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 5% to 1%, and the regime reading stayed risk-off.
